planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; give this fast-growing five-needle pine plenty of room to develop its graceful, pendulous needle display.

directions: Himalayan pine is a wide-ranging five-needle species from the mountains of Afghanistan to central China, prized in cultivation for long, soft, blue-green needles that hang in graceful drooping tufts along the branches. It grows considerably faster than most other five-needle pines when young and develops a broad, open pyramidal crown with age, eventually bearing long, slender, resin-coated cones. It prefers cool summers and consistent moisture over hot, humid conditions, and benefits from shelter from strong wind while establishing. Full sun and deep, well-drained soil suit it best, and it is a popular specimen tree in larger landscapes and arboretum pine collections.

planting.note: Plant container-grown trees in spring in full sun on well-drained soil, siting where the trunk's exfoliating bark will be visible as a winter feature as the tree matures over many decades.

directions: Lacebark pine is a slow-growing Chinese species grown chiefly for its ornamental bark, which exfoliates in patches of gray, green, and creamy white on mature trunks and limbs, creating a mottled camouflage effect prized in winter landscapes. Young trees are often multi-stemmed and shrubby, only developing the full bark display and a broad pyramidal to rounded crown after twenty or more years in the ground. It tolerates urban conditions, alkaline soil, heat, and drought once established, making it a durable long-term specimen for parks, campuses, and large home landscapes. Plant it in full sun with room to mature, since its ornamental value builds slowly over the tree's lifetime.

planting.note: Sow fresh acorns in fall or plant container-grown saplings in fall or spring in deep, well-drained soil; allow generous room for this vigorous species to reach large-tree stature.

directions: Chestnut-leaved oak is a fast-growing species native to the Caucasus and northern Iran, named for its long, deeply toothed leaves that strongly resemble sweet chestnut foliage and turn warm yellow-bronze in autumn. It develops into a large, handsome shade tree with a broad rounded crown and furrowed gray bark, growing notably faster in youth than most other oak species. It tolerates heat, some drought, and a range of soils once established, making it a reliable choice for large parks, campuses, and estate-scale plantings. Give it deep soil and full sun and plan for its eventual substantial size.

planting.note: Plant container-grown stock in fall or spring in lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; established plants shrug off summer drought and poor, rocky ground that would stress most other oaks.

directions: Kermes oak is a dense, spiny-leaved evergreen shrub or small tree of the Mediterranean basin, historically significant as the host plant of the kermes scale insect once used to produce a prized red dye. Its small, holly-like leathery leaves and tolerance of poor, rocky, lime-rich soils make it a tough, low-maintenance choice for xeriscape and Mediterranean-style gardens in mild climates. It responds well to shearing into a dense hedge or can be left to form an irregular thicket, and it resists browsing thanks to its spiny foliage. Give it full sun and sharp drainage, since it has little tolerance for wet feet or hard freezes.

planting.note: Sow fresh acorns in fall or plant container-grown saplings in fall or spring in well-drained, acidic soil; this species tolerates drier sites than most European oaks once established.

directions: Pyrenean oak is a deciduous species of southwestern Europe notable for soft, deeply lobed, gray-downy young leaves and a tendency to hold withered foliage well into winter, giving it marcescent interest in the dormant season. It forms a broad, often multi-stemmed tree and is unusually tolerant of poor, dry, acidic soils where other European oaks struggle, reflecting its native habitat on rocky Iberian hillsides. Growth is moderate and the tree is long-lived, developing rugged, deeply fissured bark with age. Plant in full sun on well-drained, lime-free ground for best results.
